finding.scope: Complex algebraic geometry with Q-coefficients; d >= 2; applies verbatim to every simply-branched Hurwitz chart over M_{0,r}, whose branch map is finite etale.
finding.statement: Reusable mechanism, independent of the tetragonal setting. Let W be a smooth connected complex d-fold admitting a dominant (in particular finite etale) morphism to M_{0,d+3}, equivalently to the complement of the diagonals in (M_{0,4})^d. Then W admits a connected finite etale cover W' with F^{d} Gr^W_{d+1} H_c^{d+1}(W';C) nonzero, hence with a non-Tate weight-equals-degree corner: pull back the mu_3-Kummer elliptic cover C -> M_{0,4} (from y^3=x(x-1), Cbar of genus one) in each of the d coordinates, take Q(-1) from one H_c^2(C) and H^{1,0}(Cbar) from the other d-1 factors, and note that every locus removed along the way has dimension <= d-1 so that F^{d} H_c^{d+1} vanishes on it and the class survives by FND-0165. Therefore no weight-equals-degree corner statement about such a base can be an etale-local statement, and no such statement can be proved by any argument that is invariant under finite etale refinement (transfer, averaging, monodromy-orbit counting, or descent along an atlas).
